name: Bosentan

fields.mechanism_of_action: Endothelin receptor antagonist (ETRA) — blocks endothelin-1 binding to ETA and ETB receptors, reducing vasoconstriction and vascular remodeling — anchored to FDA TRACLEER pharmacology review and EMA SmPC.
indications: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH; WHO Group 1) to improve exercise ability and delay clinical worsening — FDA TRACLEER label; NYHA functional class II-III and IV.
contraindications: Pregnancy (category X / embryo-fetal toxicity — mandatory pregnancy testing before initiation, monthly during therapy, and one month after discontinuation); Concurrent cyclosporine A (contraindicated); Concurrent glyburide (contraindicated — increased liver enzyme risk); Hypersensitivity; Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) — contraindicated.
side_effects: Very common (≥10%): headache, nasopharyngitis, flushing, edema (peripheral), anemia; Common (1–10%): hypotension, sinusitis, palpitations, dyspepsia, pruritus; Serious: severe hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST elevation requiring interruption/reduction), significant anemia, edema requiring diuretic management — anchored to FDA TRACLEER adverse-reactions data.

dosage.adult: Initial 62.5 mg BID for 4 weeks; maintenance 125 mg BID — FDA TRACLEER label. Dose adjustments for LFT elevations per label table.
dosage.geriatric: No specific geriatric dose adjustment; same as adult with caution due to comorbidities — FDA TRACLEER section 8.5.
dosage.paediatric: Age ≥3 years with PAH and weight ≥40 kg: 62.5 mg BID initial, 125 mg BID maintenance; weight <40 kg: 2 mg/kg BID (max 62.5 mg BID) — FDA TRACLEER pediatric section. Not recommended <3 years.

fields.adult_dosing: Initial 62.5 mg BID for 4 weeks, then 125 mg BID — anchored to FDA TRACLEER label. If LFT elevations occur, hold/reduce per label dose-modification table.
fields.pediatric_dosing: Age ≥3 years with PAH: initial 62.5 mg BID (or 2 mg/kg BID if <40 kg), maintenance 125 mg BID — FDA TRACLEER pediatric dosing section. Not recommended <3 years.
interactions: Cyclosporine A: contraindicated (increased bosentan exposure, increased cyclosporine levels); Glyburide: contraindicated (increased liver enzyme risk); CYP2C9/CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, fluconazole, amiodarone, ritonavir): may increase exposure — consider dose reduction; CYP2C9/CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin): may decrease exposure — avoid concurrent use; Simvastatin and other statins: may decrease statin levels — monitor lipids; Warfarin: no clinically significant interaction — anchored to FDA TRACLEER interactions table.
monitoring: LFTs (ALT, AST, total bilirubin): baseline, monthly, and 2 weeks after any dose increase/change — hold/reduce if ALT/AST >3×ULN; Hemoglobin: baseline, monthly, and 2 weeks after dose change; Pregnancy test: before initiation, monthly during therapy, and 1 month after discontinuation — mandatory per REMS; Blood pressure and edema assessment: baseline and regularly; Anemia signs (fatigue, pallor, dyspnea) — prompt evaluation.
patient_counselling: Take exactly twice daily (morning and evening) at same times; pregnancy testing is mandatory before starting and monthly — use two forms of effective contraception; report yellowing of eyes/skin (jaundice), dark urine, severe fatigue, or new/worsening shortness of breath; report leg/swelling changes; do not stop suddenly — discuss dose changes with clinician; avoid concurrent cyclosporine A or glyburide; avoid live vaccines unless clinician advises — anchored to FDA TRACLEER counselling framework.
warnings: Embryo-fetal toxicity (REMS-required pregnancy-prevention program); Hepatotoxicity (monthly LFT monitoring mandatory); Anemia (monitor hemoglobin; dose interruption/reduction if significant); Edema/fluid retention (treat with diuretics; dose interruption if severe); Concurrent CYP interactions; Concurrent glyburide or cyclosporine A (contraindicated) — anchored to FDA TRACLEER warnings and precautions.
precautions: Dose interruption/reduction required for hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST >3×ULN), significant anemia, and severe edema; Concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitors/inducers require dose adjustments; Concurrent statin therapy requires lipid monitoring; Concurrent warfarin does not require adjustment but standard INR monitoring continues; Pregnancy and contraception mandatory; Breast-feeding: discuss plans; Driving/machinery: caution with hypotension — anchored to FDA TRACLEER precautions.
serious_adverse_reactions: Severe hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST elevation requiring dose interruption/reduction); Significant anemia (hemoglobin decrease >1 g/dL requiring dose interruption/reduction); Severe edema/fluid retention requiring hospitalization or dose interruption; Teratospermia (potential male fertility impact); Anaphylaxis (rare) — anchored to FDA TRACLEER serious adverse reactions and clinical-trial reports.
food_interactions: May take with or without food — anchored to FDA TRACLEER administration (no food effect documented). Concurrent alcohol (additive hypotension) — standard practice rather than a specific interaction.
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Embryo-fetal toxicity (REMS-based pregnancy-prevention program required — mandatory pregnancy testing before initiation, monthly during therapy, and 1 month after discontinuation; use two forms of effective contraception) — anchored to FDA TRACLEER pregnancy and reproductive potential sections.
fields.lactation_guidance: Not established whether bosentan is present in human milk; because of potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother — anchored to FDA TRACLEER lactation section.
fields.overdose: No specific antidote; supportive management including airway protection, intravenous fluids, blood-pressure management, edema management; activated charcoal may be considered if ingestion was recent; hemodialysis not expected to be effective (high protein binding, large distribution volume) — anchored to standard PAH-agent overdose management and FDA label.
fields.pharmacokinetics: Absolute oral bioavailability ~50% (food does not significantly alter absorption); peak plasma concentration ~3–5 hours; elimination half-life ~5.4 hours (terminal half-life shorter than dosing interval, allowing BID dosing); metabolized primarily by CYP2C9 and CYP3A4; renal excretion of metabolites accounts for ~3% of dose — anchored to FDA TRACLEER clinical pharmacology.
clinical_pearls: REMS-required pregnancy-prevention program (monthly pregnancy testing mandatory); Dose interruption/reduction required for ALT/AST >3×ULN; Concurrent cyclosporine A and glyburide are absolute contraindications; Concurrent CYP inhibitors/inducers require dose adjustments; Concurrent statins require lipid monitoring — anchored to FDA TRACLEER clinical studies and administration instructions.
black_box_warnings: Embryo-fetal toxicity (REMS-based pregnancy-prevention program — mandatory pregnancy testing and effective contraception); Hepatotoxicity (monthly LFT monitoring required — dose interruption/reduction for ALT/AST >3×ULN); Risk of anemia (monitor hemoglobin); Risk of teratospermia (potential male fertility impact) — anchored to FDA TRACLEER boxed warnings.
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No dose adjustment required for renal impairment (CrCl >15 mL/min); not studied in severe renal impairment (CrCl <15 mL/min) or dialysis — anchored to FDA TRACLEER renal-impairment section; use with caution.
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: Mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A or B): no initial dose adjustment required, but monitor LFTs closely; Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C): contraindicated — anchored to FDA TRACLEER hepatic-impairment section.
fields.administration_instructions: Oral administration — 62.5 mg BID initially (4 weeks), then 125 mg BID maintenance; take with or without food; pregnancy testing mandatory before initiation, monthly during therapy, and 1 month after discontinuation — anchored to FDA TRACLEER dosage, administration, and REMS instructions.
